name: Haman
bio: Haman the Agagite, son of Hammedatha, was promoted by King Ahasuerus above all the other officials, and all the king's servants bowed to him except Mordecai, who refused as a Jew. Enraged, Haman resolved not merely to punish Mordecai but to destroy all the Jews throughout the empire. After casting lots to fix a date, he told the king that this scattered people disobeyed royal law and offered ten thousand talents of silver to fund their destruction; Ahasuerus gave him his signet ring and full authority. Haman had letters sent to every province in the king's name, ordering the annihilation of every Jew, young and old, on the thirteenth day of Adar, while he and the king celebrated and the city of Susa was thrown into distress (Esther 3:1-15). His downfall, engineered through Esther and Mordecai, is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
